comparisons.peer_summary: GS&Co. is a defendant in a putative class action filed in August 2021 alleging an antitrust conspiracy to manipulate foreign exchange auctions; in May 2023, certain state common law claims were dismissed while remaining claims survived, leading plaintiffs to file a second amended complaint in July 2023 seeking unspecified treble damages.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citibank (C) and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose pending putative class action litigation alleging antitrust conspiracy to manipulate foreign exchange markets. Citibank faces a specific action in the Federal Court of Australia filed in 2019, whereas Goldman Sachs faces a similar antitrust conspiracy claim regarding FX auctions filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York in August 2021. Both lawsuits seek treble or compensatory damages and injunctive relief, reflecting industry-wide exposure to FX manipulation allegations.

sentences.text: In 2019, a putative class action was filed against Citibank and other defendants, captioned J WISBEY & ASSOCIATES PTY LTD v. UBS AG & ORS, in the Federal Court of Australia.
Plaintiffs assert claims under antitrust laws and seek compensatory damages and declaratory and injunctive relief.
GS&Co. is among the defendants named in a putative class action filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York on August 4, 2021.

The amended complaint, filed on January 6, 2022, generally asserts claims under federal antitrust law and state common law in connection with an alleged conspiracy among the defendants to manipulate auctions for foreign exchange transactions on an electronic trading platform, as well as claims under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act.
The complaint seeks declaratory and injunctive relief, as well as unspecified amounts of treble and other damages.

comparisons.peer_summary: India's Enforcement Directorate is investigating J.P. While most FX-related settlements are complete, a South Africa Competition Commission matter remains pending, and civil litigation continues in the U.K., Israel, and other jurisdictions with specific developments including a U.K. class certification overturn and an Israeli settlement in principle.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citibank and JPMorgan Chase disclose that civil litigation related to foreign exchange remains pending. Specifically, Citibank discloses a putative class action in Australia alleging FX market manipulation, while JPMorgan Chase explicitly states that FX-related individual and putative class actions filed outside the U.S., including in Australia, remain active. This highlights a shared risk profile regarding historical FX trading practices in international jurisdictions.
